data.name: Tales of Adventure 2
data.detailed_description:
Tales of Adventure 2 is a 2D shoot’em up with over 30 different stylistic levels and
exciting mechanics. Defeat the enemy and gain power-up crystals to advance your stats and
abilities. Loot the most exotic items to defeat the enemy!

Features

  • 30+ levels each with its unique mechanics.
  • 40+ types of monsters with unique behaviors and attack animation.
  • All monsters tell you a little about this new world; together, these pieces of
    information define this world.
  • 12 tracks of BGM.
  • Consuming power-up crystals will randomly boost your attributes.
  • 8 types of spells. Upgrading spells also changes animation. When you upgrade your low
    level spells, there’s a chance you will discover a new spell!
  • Items will periodically spawn in your screen, don’t miss them!
  • Special effects from spells and items can stack. Find out the best combination to
    annihilate the enemy!

data.short_description: Set in a mysterious yet dangerous fantasy world, you have to constantly grow stronger to defeat the powerful monsters on your journey. Magical items will also randomly appear and aid you in your adventure.

reviews.review:
Tales of Adventure 2 is a compact indie action game that combines 2D shoot ’em up combat with RPG-style character growth, randomized upgrades, magic, item collection, and a fantasy setting. Developed by XIAOYAO and BetaSparkUK and published by XIAOYAO, it is built around a relatively simple premise: fight through numerous stages, eliminate increasingly varied creatures, collect useful resources, and gradually transform the playable character into a much more capable fighter. It does not attempt to compete with large-scale action RPGs in presentation or narrative complexity, instead focusing its energy on arcade-style progression and experimentation.

Combat forms the heart of the experience. Players move through stages while attacking enemies, avoiding their offensive patterns, and looking for opportunities to collect items and upgrades. The shoot ’em up influence gives encounters a faster rhythm than the game's RPG elements might initially suggest. Positioning and reaction speed matter, especially when multiple enemies occupy the screen. With more than 30 levels to work through, the campaign attempts to maintain variety by giving stages their own characteristics and mechanics rather than simply repeating the same arena with stronger opponents.

Enemy diversity contributes significantly to this structure. More than 40 monster types are included, with creatures featuring different behaviors and attack animations. Learning what individual opponents can do becomes increasingly useful as the difficulty develops. This variety prevents combat from relying entirely on inflated statistics, since recognizing enemy behavior can be just as important as improving the protagonist. Monsters also contribute pieces of information about the world, allowing elements of the setting and its background to emerge through encounters rather than depending exclusively on lengthy dialogue or conventional exposition.

Character improvement revolves partly around power-up crystals. Consuming these crystals can randomly increase attributes, creating an element of unpredictability in progression. This works particularly well for players who enjoy adapting to whatever bonuses they receive rather than following a rigid character build. The drawback is that random development can occasionally make progression feel less controlled. Players who prefer carefully optimizing every statistic may find this approach frustrating, but the randomness fits the game's arcade-oriented philosophy and gives individual stretches of progression some variation.

Magic adds another worthwhile layer to the combat system. Eight spell types are available, and upgrading them can affect more than their raw effectiveness. Their animations can change as they become stronger, while developing lower-level magic can also lead to the discovery of additional spells. This provides a sense of experimentation because investing in basic abilities can produce something beyond a predictable numerical increase. The spell system is not exceptionally complicated, but it gives players another reason to continue improving their character and testing different offensive possibilities.

Items appearing during gameplay further expand the potential combinations. Players must pay attention to pickups while simultaneously managing enemies and incoming attacks, making awareness an important part of successful play. More importantly, item and spell effects can stack. Combining multiple bonuses can lead to substantially more powerful attacks and creates some satisfying moments when a collection of modest improvements develops into a highly effective setup. Discovering useful combinations is one of the more enjoyable aspects of the progression system and provides an incentive to engage with pickups rather than treating them as disposable bonuses.

The presentation is considerably more modest than the underlying collection of mechanics. Its visuals carry the unmistakable character of a small retro-inspired indie production, and animation, interfaces, effects, and environmental detail are relatively basic by modern standards. That simplicity can have some nostalgic appeal, particularly for players familiar with older independent PC games, but anyone expecting highly polished contemporary graphics will need to adjust expectations. The soundtrack offers 12 background music tracks, providing some musical variation across the adventure without overwhelming the action.

Repetition is ultimately the game's most notable weakness. Despite the number of stages, monsters, spells, and upgrade opportunities, the basic routine remains centered on fighting, collecting resources, strengthening abilities, and moving forward. Players who enjoy incremental improvement and experimenting with stacked effects are likely to remain engaged longer than those seeking constant mechanical reinvention. The RPG elements add welcome depth, but this remains primarily an arcade action experience rather than a deep role-playing game.

Steam Deck compatibility is not officially verified by Valve, so it should not be treated as a fully certified Steam Deck title. Its relatively lightweight 2D design makes it the sort of game that may be playable through Steam Deck's Proton compatibility layer, but unofficial operation can involve controller configuration, interface issues, or other compatibility quirks. Players specifically purchasing it for handheld use should therefore consider its Steam Deck status unverified rather than guaranteed.

Taken on its own terms, Tales of Adventure 2 has a surprising number of ideas packed into a relatively humble package. Randomized character improvements, evolving spells, dozens of enemy types, stackable effects, item pickups, and more than 30 stages give it greater mechanical variety than its straightforward presentation initially suggests. It lacks the refinement and depth of stronger examples from either the shoot ’em up or RPG genres, but its combination of arcade action and persistent progression can still provide an entertaining experience for players attracted to obscure, experimental indie games.

Rating: 5/10
